name: Command Line & Dev Tools
description: Basic navigation in the terminal, managing files, and using browser developer tools.
toolingExplanation: The terminal is a text-based window where you give commands to your computer instead of clicking icons. DevTools in Chrome or Edge let you inspect web pages.

name: HTML5 Fundamentals
description: Structure of web pages using semantic HTML tags, headings, forms, and accessibility basics.
toolingExplanation: HTML files (.html) are plain text files that browsers interpret to show headings, paragraphs, buttons, and links.

name: CSS3 Styling & Box Model
description: Styling web pages, colors, fonts, margins, padding, borders, and CSS selectors.
toolingExplanation: CSS files (.css) tell the browser how HTML elements should look: their colors, spacing, and sizing.

name: Responsive Web Design & Flexbox
description: Building layouts that adjust seamlessly to mobile phones, tablets, and desktops using Flexbox and media queries.
toolingExplanation: Media queries and flexible layout boxes ensure your site looks great on small smartphone screens as well as laptops.

name: Git & GitHub Version Control
description: Tracking code changes with Git, creating commits, branches, and publishing repositories to GitHub.
toolingExplanation: Git is like a save-game system for your code. GitHub is a free website where you store and showcase your code online.

name: Modern JavaScript (ES6+)
description: Variables, data types, loops, functions, DOM manipulation, events, and modern array methods.
toolingExplanation: JavaScript runs inside the browser and makes web pages interactive, like handling clicks, form validation, and animations.

name: Async JavaScript & Fetch API
description: Promises, async/await, and making HTTP network requests to external APIs using fetch.
toolingExplanation: Async code lets your webpage load information from servers across the internet without freezing the user interface.

name: React Fundamentals & Components
description: Component-driven development, JSX, props, state with useState, and effects with useEffect.
toolingExplanation: React is a popular library for building reusable UI components, powering modern web applications.

name: Node.js & Express API Development
description: Building backend HTTP servers, routing, middleware, and JSON REST endpoints.
toolingExplanation: Node.js lets you run JavaScript on a computer or server outside the browser to build APIs and handle business logic.

name: MongoDB & Database Modeling
description: Document databases, MongoDB Atlas, Mongoose schemas, queries, and CRUD operations.
toolingExplanation: MongoDB is a database that stores your application's data in flexible JSON-like documents.

name: RESTful API Design & Auth
description: Designing clean REST APIs, HTTP status codes, user authentication with JWT, and input validation.
toolingExplanation: REST APIs provide standard endpoints where frontends and mobile apps can securely send and receive data.
